title: Compute-optimal data scaling for neural surrogates via multi-fidelity training
claim: Splitting data into budget and fidelity mixture yields optimal mixtures that match high-fidelity-only accuracy with far less generation compute.
layout: 3 zones: central 3D error surface, mixture insets below, three result plots right
description: The figure has a legend at the top: a green star line for the optimal mixture (λ*) and a dashed orange line for high-fidelity only. On the left is a 3D error surface with a vertical colorbar (purple for high error, yellow for low). The surface is plotted over a Fidelity mixture (λ) axis and a Budget axis. A green starred path follows the optimal mixture across it, and an orange dotted path runs along the high-fidelity edge. Below the surface, three rounded boxes show airfoil meshes. λ→-∞ is many cheap coarse samples, λ=0 is a uniform mixture, and λ→∞ is a few expensive fine samples. Dashed arrows link these boxes to positions on the fidelity axis. A large arrow points right to three stacked log-scale Error-vs-Budget plots. Each has a small PDE inset: a turbulence-like blob, a flow field with obstacles, and an airfoil. The green curves lie below the orange ones, and a 6.3× annotation marks the compute savings.
caption: Overview of our multi-fidelity data scaling approach. We split the data axis into generation budget and fidelity mixture, parametrized by $\lambda$. Bottom: example discretization fidelity mixtures. Right: Across diverse settings, multi-fidelity training at optimal mixtures (green) reaches the error of high-fidelity-only training (orange, dashed) with up to $6.3\times$ less data generation compute.
abstract: Neural surrogates for Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) are usually trained on synthetic data from numerical simulators. As models grow and scaling laws demand larger datasets, the cost of data generation often outweighs the training cost and becomes the bottleneck in the scaling quest. Unlike data in other domains, however, each PDE sample has a tunable cost that depends on its numerical fidelity, with the resulting cost-accuracy trade-off governed by known convergence rates. We exploit this property by formalizing neural surrogate training as a function of both data quantity and fidelity under a fixed data generation compute budget, treating fidelity as a fine-grained discrete spectrum rather than a binary distinction. Building on this, we show that multi-fidelity training enables Pareto-optimal error scaling against data generation compute. By using simulations at lower fidelities as an additional training signal, training on the optimal fidelity mixture matches the accuracy of high-fidelity-only training, with up to $6.3\times$ less data generation compute across our settings. We validate these findings across six PDE problems spanning structured grids and unstructured meshes, two distinct error sources (discretization and iterative-solver error), and four surrogate architectures, totaling over 7,000 training runs.
